title: The walk home
hook: the old rite that ended a student's years with the teacher, and its last words: treat the guest as God
carry: speak truth, live dharma, honor the guest as god
tomorrow: The Isha Upanishad: all this is pervaded by the Lord

segments.voice: Yesterday, anasakti: Gandhi's Gita, the battle inside. Your line was act fully, don't cling to the fruit. Today, the last day of this long stretch with the Gita.

In ancient India, a student lived for years in the teacher's house, learning the Vedas by heart, tending the fire, fetching water. When the studies were done, there was a rite called samavartana: the return home. The student bathed, put on new clothes, and the teacher gave a last talk. One version of that talk survives in the Taittiriya Upanishad. Then the student walked home, carrying it all. Today is your samavartana.
screen: `YEARS IN THE TEACHER'S HOUSE.` → `A BATH, NEW CLOTHES.` → `THEN, THE WALK HOME.`

segments.voice: The teacher's talk is still one of the best-known passages in Hinduism. Satyam vada: speak the truth. Dharmam chara: live by dharma. Don't neglect your study, the svadhyaya from two days ago. And then four short lines many Indian children still learn: matri devo bhava, pitri devo bhava, acharya devo bhava, atithi devo bhava. Let your mother be as God to you. Your father. Your teacher. And your guest. That last one is why, in so many Hindu homes, a guest is fed first and fed too much: the guest at the door is treated as the divine come to visit. Notice where the teaching sends the student. Not to a cave. Home: to parents, to guests, to a household. In Hindu thought, the student's years are one stage of life, and they open into the householder's life of dharma, lived at home. That's where these weeks with the Gita lead too. A man who drops his bow, and the same man standing up. Refuge, and do not grieve. Victory where God and the human act together. Three roads. Verses carried by heart, and studied again. Act fully, and let go of the fruit. Plenty of people keep a Gita on a shelf and never read it through; you walked it, one piece at a time. Tomorrow the path goes deeper, into the Upanishads, the texts the Gita draws on, starting with the Isha: all this is pervaded by the Lord. But today, like the student, take the bath, put on the new clothes, and walk home with it.
screen: `SATYAM VADA. DHARMAM CHARA.` · `ATITHI DEVO BHAVA: THE GUEST AS GOD.` · `NOT TO A CAVE. HOME.` · `LOOKING BACK AT THE GITA.` · then, large: `THE WALK HOME.`

segments.voice: Picture the student's last morning: the bath, the new clothes, the teacher's last words. Now think of the home you'll walk into today. Choose one of the teacher's lines for it: speak the truth, or treat the next person at your door as you'd treat God. If you pray, ask for help keeping it; if not, just hold the intention. Then walk home with your one Gita verse.
Graduation. In the old tradition, samavartana, the student's return home, with a last teaching: speak the truth, live by dharma, honor the guest as God.
Your line: speak truth, live dharma, honor the guest as God. The teacher's last words, carried home. Camp four, complete.

howItsDone: In traditional Hindu education, the end of study was marked by samavartana, the student's ceremonial return home; the teacher's final advice in Taittiriya Upanishad 1.11 is still recited at some convocations in India, and 'atithi devo bhava', the guest is as God, is still taught to children and lived at many Hindu tables.
